meta.note: Visual brief for the 'four university rankings disagree' story. Spine: 'best university' is a weighting choice, not a fact. Theme = editorial_dark, gilt-gold crown accent, didone_fashion type, nocturne BGM + night-campus cinematic. Hero = an ANIMATED ETH Zurich night panorama (real_still + image2video) that butts the 'four tables, four champions' hook right up against it. In-body centerpiece = the reweighter explorable at edt_06 (ana_12). 13 cover-able landscape campus photos registered (6 sct_ + 7 des_) to feed the mandatory cinematic scroll.

media_strategy.selection_principle: All five channels earn a place on a data-driven basis (chart, image, video, audio, interactive). Nothing is added to tick a channel; a static world map is deliberately NOT used because no country-aggregated data_table supports it.
media_strategy.chart_variety: bump -> heatmap -> dumbbell/range -> 100%-stacked bar -> diverging bar -> scatter -> grouped lollipop -> 2-point slope -> dot plot. No two adjacent sections repeat a chart form; no chart streak.

chart.reason: The whole story is a set of reproducible rank comparisons — nine distinct chart forms carry the spine (disagreement matrix, swingers, four champions, referee scatter, weighting shares, size flip).

image.reason: Real, verified campus photographs (Detective ref_ + Scout sct_) ground the named cast (Peking/Tsinghua/Berkeley/Caltech/Michigan/Toronto/UCL/Washington) and back the cinematic scroll. No AI-faked campuses.

video.reason: The richness floor requires an animated hero on this visual topic. A subtle cinemagraph of the real ETH Zurich night panorama (image2video on a verified still, subject held) opens the page with motion; it pairs with the nocturne BGM.

audio.reason: Mandatory BGM. Scout-sourced John Field Nocturne (CC-BY-SA-4.0, rung 1 sourced_bgm) as a top-of-article now-playing card with a real (non-AI) Bosendorfer-keyboard cover; pensive tone matches the sober/analytical subject. Never autoplay; page works muted.

interactive_or_map.reason: The reweighter (ana_12) is the in-body centerpiece — the reader manufactures Oxford/MIT/Michigan as #1 from the same data. Six curated supporting playgrounds (Editor's interactives block) cover distinct findings. A static country CHOROPLETH is NOT used: no clean country-aggregated data_table over the 218-core exists (only per-named-school country labels), so a map would be decorative rather than INFORM — the exploration channel is carried by the interactives.

team_brief.centerpiece_note: The reweighter explorable MUST render and be usable BEFORE the paragraph that names Oxford (87.02) / MIT (96.25) / Michigan (100.0). It recomputes on the Analyst's audited code/client_model.js:reweightRankings so the live #1 and the prose figures are two readouts of one model.
team_brief.cinematic_note: 13 verified, license-clean, landscape (cover-able) campus backgrounds are registered (6 Scout sct_ + 7 Designer des_). All resolve to a complete license+identity block (sct_ blocks in scout.json; des_ blocks inline below). ETH is the hero (cin_00). The 3 crests (des_crest_*) are logos, NOT counted toward the landscape floor.

des_hero_video.label: Animated hero — ETH Zurich night panorama

content.hero_why: Rung 1 (interactive hero) is reserved for the in-body reweighter centerpiece — the hook here should be a single wide, atmospheric campus image, not a widget. Rung 2 (real_still) fits: elite universities ARE concrete photographable subjects, and a verified ultra-wide night panorama of ETH Zurich's Hauptgebaude (sct_eth, 10060x2636, CC-BY-SA-3.0) is a strong cover-able face of the story that carries zero real-person risk. Animate it into a subtle cinemagraph (image2video) so the cover moves — a static still would fail the richness floor on this visual topic.
content.model: kwaivgi/kling-v3.0-std (or veo-3.1-fast default — no real human face is present, only a building, so either is safe; Hero role picks)
content.motion_prompt: Subtle cinemagraph: the night sky drifts almost imperceptibly, the warm interior window-lights and the lit central rotunda flicker gently, faint atmospheric haze moves; the neoclassical building itself is held perfectly still with no warp or camera shake; slow ~4% parallax push-in toward the lit dome. Motion visible-at-a-glance but calm, matching a nocturne.
content.disclosure: Image = a real Wikimedia Commons photograph of ETH Zurich (not AI). Motion = a subtle camera push + atmospheric light/sky animation added to the still; not AI video of a person.
content.hook_landing: The Programmer overlays the working headline ('Who Is the Best University in the World? Pick a Number.') plus a compact right-against-the-image stat strip that names the surprise immediately — 'Four rankings. Four different #1s. Caltech - Harvard - MIT - Michigan.' — so the reader meets the hook in the first beat, before scrolling. Use a solid scrim/plate to hold WCAG AA over the night image.

des_hero_video.brief: Full-bleed cinematic hero band: the ETH Zurich Hauptgebaude at night (lit domed rotunda, symmetric colonnaded wings, empty forecourt) animated as a restrained cinemagraph that loops seamlessly (boomerang). The night mood pairs with the John Field nocturne BGM card directly below. The Hero role (Stage 4.6) renders assets/teaser.webm + _web.mp4 + .jpg poster from the verified still and reuses data-des="des_hero_video".
des_hero_video.rationale: Real-subject rule: ETH is a specific real landmark, so it must be a FETCHED verified still, never generated. Animating a fetched still (no faces) into a cinemagraph is sanctioned and clears the animated-hero richness floor. An ultra-wide night panorama is the single most cover-able, nocturne-matched asset in the set.

content.trigger: Starts on the reader's first scroll or first click (NEVER autoplay). Page works fully when muted.
content.ui_form: Top-of-article now-playing card with a spinning-vinyl treatment: the real Bosendorfer-keyboard cover (sct_bgm_cover) is the rotating disc, the eyebrow 'Now playing' sits above the piece title, a play/pause control and a mute-safe visual equaliser. Placed at the very top of edt_01 so the reader can start it before reading.
content.fallback: Muted/unsupported: the card shows the static cover + a disabled play affordance with a tooltip; nothing on the page depends on audio.
content.novelty_note: Not a bolted-on tone card — the nocturne is a deliberate signature bed for a scholarly-nocturne page, thematically tied to the night-campus hero and cinematic scroll.

des_bgm.brief: A self-hosted, cover-art now-playing card at the very top of the article. Cover = the real ornate Bosendorfer grand-piano keyboard (Scout-verified, non-AI). Click/scroll to start; loops quietly under the reading.
des_bgm.rationale: Mandatory BGM, rung 1 (sourced_bgm) — the Scout found a license-clean real recording (CC-BY-SA-4.0) whose OWN license was verified (also satisfies the rung-C classical floor). Web-weight mp3 (<3 MB) via optimize_assets; media_ref keeps license/identity in scout.json.

des_champions.label: Four tables, four champions (bump)

content.reshape: From ana_06.data_table (rows = rank 1..10, columns = THE_2015 / ARWU_2015 / CWUR_2015 / QS_2023 / OpenAlex_works, each cell a university short-name), build a tidy {university, system, rank} table: for each of the 15 distinct names that reach any top-10, its rank in each system where it appears in the top 10 (absent = no point that column).
content.x: system, as an ORDERED axis along the perception->output axis: QS_2023, THE_2015, CWUR_2015, ARWU_2015, OpenAlex_works (survey pole -> output pole -> neutral referee)
content.y: rank (1 at TOP, inverted scale, domain 1..10)

highlight.rule: Spend the gold --accent on the four different rank-1 holders; give the five all-four-top-10 schools a consistent muted trace colour so the eye can follow them shuffling; grey everything else.

content.annotate: Mark the four rank-1 slots where the line changes hands across the axis (MIT -> Caltech -> Harvard -> Michigan). One short callout at the OpenAlex column: 'the neutral referee crowns a fifth winner.'
content.interaction: Hover a line to lift it and label the school + its rank in each system; hover a rank-1 node to show the system name.

style.scheme: gold accent + neutral traces on dark

des_champions.brief: The signature opener: a bump chart across the five ranking systems (ordered survey->output->neutral). Four different lines touch the #1 slot as the axis moves right — the visual proof that no school is #1 everywhere. Only five lines run the full width inside the top 10; the rest appear and vanish.
des_champions.rationale: Ranking intent across multiple conditions -> slope/bump (chart_chooser ranking.slope_chart). The changing-hands at rank 1 is exactly the hook 'four tables, four champions', and ordering x on the perception->output axis makes the crossing meaningful, not arbitrary.

des_corr_matrix.label: How far apart they are (Spearman heatmap)

content.reshape: ana_04.data_table gives the 6 unique pairs (system_a, system_b, spearman). Mirror them into a symmetric 4x4 matrix (THE/ARWU/CWUR/QS) and set the diagonal to 1.0. Order the systems so QS sits at the edge (e.g. ARWU, CWUR, THE, QS) so the systematic outlier reads as a low-value band.
content.color: spearman (sequential CVD-safe ramp 'cividis', domain fixed to [0.55, 1.0] so the 0.60-0.85 differences are visible; diagonal 1.0 sits at the top of the ramp)
content.text: the Spearman value printed in every cell (redundant encoding — color is decodable without memory)

highlight.most_alike: ARWU x CWUR = 0.853 (both survey-free research tables)
highlight.least_alike: CWUR x QS = 0.599 (the survey-free table vs the survey table)
highlight.outlier_band: the whole QS row/column (0.599 / 0.647 / 0.735 — the three lowest of six)

content.annotate: Outline the QS row+column and label it 'the reputation-survey pole agrees least with everyone'. Ring the CWUR x QS cell (0.599) as the single lowest.
content.interaction: Hover a cell for the pair + exact Spearman + Kendall (from data_table).

des_corr_matrix.brief: A 4x4 correlation heatmap of the commercial systems. Warm/light = agree, dark = diverge. The QS band reads darkest; the ARWU-CWUR cell lightest. Numbers printed in every cell.
des_corr_matrix.rationale: Relationship between two categorical variables (system x system) with a value per cell -> xy_heatmap (chart_chooser correlation). A fixed narrow colour domain plus in-cell numbers keeps the 0.6-0.85 spread legible and CVD-safe.

des_swingers_dumbbell.label: The swingers — same school, tens of places apart

content.reshape: For each university in ana_05b.data_table, plot its four commercial ranks (the_rank, arwu_rank, cwur_rank, qs_rank) as four dots on a shared rank axis, connected by a thin bar from its MIN to its MAX rank (= the spread). Sort universities by spread descending.
content.y: university (sorted by spread, biggest swing at top)
content.x: rank (1 = best, at LEFT; log or capped-linear to ~200 since this is the band-free <=200 set)
content.dot_color: system (THE / ARWU / CWUR / QS) — categorical CVD-safe (Okabe-Ito subset); each dot labelled/shaped so system is readable without colour alone
content.connector: a muted bar from min to max rank per school = the spread

highlight.rule: Accent the Peking and Tsinghua bars in gold (the cleanest reputation-vs-research swing); show Berkeley as the reverse-direction swinger; leave the tight anchors (Harvard/MIT/Oxford) as short grey bars to contrast a flat top.

content.annotate: Pin '89 places' on Peking's bar between its QS dot and its ARWU dot; a one-line note 'QS survey lifts them ~90 places above ARWU's prizes metric.'
content.interaction: Hover a school to read all four ranks + spread; hover a dot for the system name.

des_swingers_dumbbell.brief: A dumbbell/range plot: each famous school is a row; its four commercial ranks are dots spread along the axis, joined by a bar whose length IS the disagreement. Peking and Tsinghua stretch nearly the full width; Harvard and MIT barely move. Band-free set only (schools <=200 in all four) so no tail-band artefacts.
des_swingers_dumbbell.rationale: The point is the MAGNITUDE of each school's spread and WHICH table places it where -> a sorted dumbbell/dot-strip (chart_chooser ranking.dot_strip / distribution.dot_strip) reads the spread as a length and keeps every system visible. Deliberately NOT a second bump chart (avoids a chart streak with des_champions).

des_weights.label: The weighting dial — reputation vs measured output

content.y: system (QS 2023, THE, ARWU, CWUR, OpenAlex), sorted by reputation-survey share DESCENDING so QS is at the top and the survey-free tables at the bottom
content.color: component category; but the reputation_survey segment gets the gold --accent in every bar and the other five components read as muted neutral tints, so the eye compares 'how much gold' per system

highlight.rule: Reputation-survey = gold. QS = 50% gold; THE = 33%; ARWU / CWUR / OpenAlex = 0% gold. Print the reputation % at the end of each bar (redundant encoding).

content.annotate: A bracket spanning QS's gold half labelled 'half of a QS score is surveyed opinion'; a '0%' tag on ARWU/CWUR/OpenAlex. A small footnote flag on QS 2023: 'pre-2024 legacy weights (Academic Reputation 40%)' — edition-specific (Copywriter writes the caption text).
content.interaction: Hover a segment for the exact component + percentage.

des_weights.brief: A 100%-stacked horizontal bar per system, sorted by how much of the score is surveyed reputation. The gold reputation band is half of QS, a third of THE, and vanishes entirely for ARWU, CWUR and OpenAlex — the mechanical reason they disagree, in one read.
des_weights.rationale: Composition of each score into weighted parts -> 100%-stacked bar (chart_chooser part_to_whole). Colouring only the reputation segment turns a busy stack into a single comparison: the gold quantity IS the story.

des_rep_research.label: The survey and the microscope lift different schools

content.x: qs_minus_arwu (signed gap; NEGATIVE = QS ranks it higher = reputation-lifted; POSITIVE = ARWU ranks it higher = research-lifted), diverging around a zero line
content.y: university, sorted by qs_minus_arwu (most reputation-lifted at one end, most research-lifted at the other)
content.color: direction (reputation-lifted vs research-lifted) on a CVD-safe DIVERGING ramp (blue <-> orange, NOT red-green); sign + side + label back up the colour

highlight.rule: Let the two extremes read; anchor on a labelled zero line.

content.annotate: A zero rule labelled 'same rank in both'. A standalone stat beside the chart: 'Inside QS itself, the Academic-Reputation score and Citations-per-Faculty correlate just 0.421.' (qs_internal_ar_vs_cpf_spearman from the data_table).
content.interaction: Hover a bar for the school's ARWU rank, QS rank, gap, and its QS AR / CPF sub-scores.

des_rep_research.brief: A diverging bar chart: schools QS lifts far above ARWU point one way (Asia-Pacific reputation names — HKU, NUS, Peking, Tsinghua), schools ARWU lifts far above QS point the other (US research-heavy names — Vanderbilt, Maryland, UCSB). One rewards being admired, the other rewards measured research.
des_rep_research.rationale: Signed deviation from a baseline (QS rank minus ARWU rank) -> diverging bar (chart_chooser deviation). CVD-safe blue<->orange plus the sign/side/label satisfies redundant encoding.

des_reweighter.label: CENTERPIECE — set the weights, watch #1 flip

content.client_model: code/client_model.js :: reweightRankings(weights, topN)  [consumed by the Interaction Engineer]
content.initial_state: Five labelled 0-10 sliders — Reputation, Citations, Teaching, International, Output — start at the BALANCED preset (all equal). A live leaderboard of the top ~15 of the 218 universities renders beside/below them, with a big '#1: University of Oxford - 87.02' headline card. Five preset chips sit above the sliders: Balanced / QS-like / THE-like / ARWU-like / Output-only.
content.trigger: The reader drags any slider OR taps a preset chip.
content.transition: On every change, call reweightRankings(weights) and re-sort the 218 rows live (closed-form, <1ms). The leaderboard rows animate to their new positions with a short crossfade (reuse the .embed opacity crossfade so it updates, not flickers); the '#1' card updates its name + score. When the CHAMPION actually changes (not on every drag), the crown badge does a single gentle pop (--ease-spring, once) — a rare celebratory beat, not on high-frequency slider motion.
content.payoff: The presets alone crown THREE different schools from the SAME data: Balanced -> Oxford (87.02), QS-like -> MIT (96.25), Output-only -> Michigan (100.0) [THE-like -> MIT 95.16; ARWU-like -> Michigan 95.24]. A running readout says 'You just crowned ___' so the reader realises they manufactured a world #1 by moving sliders. This lands BEFORE the prose names Oxford/MIT/Michigan.

des_reweighter.brief: The load-bearing explorable. Five real 0-100 pillars per university, blended live under reader-set weights, re-ranking all 218 schools. The reader produces the thesis with their own hands: 'best' is a slider position. It is the page's centrepiece and must be usable before the reveal paragraph. The Interaction Engineer (Stage 4.5) builds it against reweightRankings; the Hero may sit the ETH backdrop behind it.
des_reweighter.rationale: The centerpiece is a derived/model finding the reader should PRODUCE -> explorable_recompute (interaction_playbook centerpiece_doctrine). It consumes the Analyst's audited client_model so the widget's live #1 and the prose figures are two readouts of one model.

des_referee_scatter.label: The referee reorders everyone (scatter)

content.x: oa_works_rank (OpenAlex raw-output order — the neutral referee), 1 = most output
content.y: qs_rank (the most survey-driven commercial table), 1 = best
content.reference: a y = x diagonal ('if the referee agreed with QS'); points far OFF the diagonal are schools the referee reorders

focal: Michigan (OpenAlex works #1, QS 25 — the raw-output giant no commercial table crowns)
Caltech (OpenAlex works #82, QS 6 — tiny but citation-dense)
highlight.rule: Accent Michigan and Caltech in gold with direct text labels (they are the two-sided illustration); mute the rest; label a few anchors (Harvard, Oxford) that sit near the diagonal.

content.annotate: Label the diagonal 'agree'. A callout on Michigan ('#1 by output, nobody's commercial #1') and Caltech ('#1-ish commercially, #82 by output').
content.interaction: Hover a point for the school's OpenAlex works rank and its four commercial ranks.

des_referee_scatter.brief: A scatter of the neutral OpenAlex output order (x) against a commercial table (y) for the named cast. Points hug the diagonal only for the big-and-dense anchors; Michigan sits bottom-left-of-line (output #1 but commercially mid-pack) and Caltech top-right-of-line (commercially elite but output #82) — the referee crowns a different order.
des_referee_scatter.rationale: Relationship between two rank variables -> scatter (chart_chooser correlation). The y=x diagonal turns 'disagreement with the referee' into visible off-diagonal distance; the two annotated outliers are the section's whole argument.

des_referee_track.label: Which table tracks output (grouped lollipop)

content.y: commercial system (THE / ARWU / CWUR / QS), sorted by best fit
content.group: OpenAlex lens (vs_works_count / vs_cited_by / vs_h_index) — three dots per system on a thin stem, categorical CVD-safe colour + shape
content.reference: a rule at Spearman = 1.0 labelled 'perfect agreement' — so even the closest fit (ARWU 0.876) visibly falls short

highlight.closest: ARWU vs h_index = 0.876 (tracks measured impact most)
highlight.loosest: QS vs h_index = 0.636 (the reputation table tracks impact least)
highlight.rule: Accent ARWU's high dot and QS's low dot; label both; the gap to the 1.0 line is the point.

content.annotate: One note near the 1.0 rule: 'even the best fit, 0.88, is far from a perfect 1.0 — the referee vindicates no single table.'
content.interaction: Hover a dot for the exact Spearman on that lens.

des_referee_track.brief: A grouped lollipop: each commercial system gets three dots (its correlation with OpenAlex works, citations, and h-index). ARWU and CWUR cluster right (they track output); QS sits left (it tracks impact least). A 1.0 reference line shows even the tightest fit stops well short of matching the referee.
des_referee_track.rationale: Comparing a small set of precomputed correlation MAGNITUDES across groups -> grouped dot/lollipop (chart_chooser magnitude.lollipop) reads the values on a common position scale, and the 1.0 reference line carries the 'still not 1.0' caveat visually.

des_size_flip.label: The size trap — volume vs impact per paper (slope)

content.x: two positions: 'By volume' (rank_volume) on the left, 'Per paper' (rank_impact) on the right
content.y: rank (1 at TOP, inverted); a line connects each school's volume rank to its impact rank

highlight.focal_plunge: Michigan: volume #1 -> impact #332 (a +331-place plunge, the steepest downward slope)
highlight.both: Harvard (#2 -> #1, the rare big-and-dense school, nearly flat at the top)
highlight.rule: Accent Michigan's plunging line in gold; show the small-dense schools' upward slopes in a second colour; keep Harvard flat at the top.

content.annotate: Pin '+331 places' on Michigan's line; label the two columns 'count papers' vs 'count impact per paper'.
content.interaction: Hover a line for the school's works_count, cites/work, and both ranks.

des_size_flip.brief: A two-point slope chart. Switch the metric from raw volume to impact-per-paper and the lines cross violently: Michigan dives from #1 to #332, while tiny citation-dense Caltech, Princeton and MIT climb from the 80s-100s into the teens. Harvard alone stays pinned near the top on both. One normalisation choice moves 'best research' by hundreds of places.
des_size_flip.rationale: Rank at two conditions (volume vs per-paper) -> slope chart (chart_chooser ranking.slope_chart). Two x-positions only, so it reads distinctly from the multi-condition bump opener and the dumbbell — no chart streak.

des_validation.label: Disagreement survives holding the year fixed (dot plot)

content.y: pair (the three same-year 2015 pairs + the three QS-2023-involving pairs)
content.color: era (same year 2015 vs 2023-vs-2015) — categorical, redundant with a shape + the y-grouping
reference: a rule at the 2015-trio mean 0.782 ('same-year agreement')
a rule at the QS mean 0.660

highlight.rule: Group the three 2015 pairs together (era held fixed) and show they still sit 0.75-0.84 — far below 1.0. Tag the QS pairs as the era-mixed set.
highlight.honest_caveat: Label the QS pairs '2023 vs 2015 — mixes method AND an ~8-year drift; read as an UPPER bound on QS's method gap, not a clean measurement.'

content.annotate: Callout on the 2015 cluster: 'even within one year, the tables agree only ~0.78 — the disagreement is about method, not the calendar.'
content.interaction: Hover a dot for the pair, Spearman, Kendall, era and n.

des_validation.brief: The 'why believe this' beat. A dot plot of the six correlations, split into the same-year 2015 trio (era held fixed) and the QS-2023 set. The 2015 trio still averages 0.782, nowhere near 1.0 — so the headline disagreement is methodological, not a year-mixing artefact. The QS set is honestly flagged as conflating method with an eight-year drift.
des_validation.rationale: Comparing correlation values across two labelled groups with honest reference lines -> dot plot with reference rules (chart_chooser comparison + annotation_layers threshold lines). Keeps the validation sober and precise.

des_scale.label: Common-core scale stat

content.label: universities in the five-system common core (a normalised-name join; treat ~200 as the scale, not a precise constant)

des_scale.brief: A single large stat in the methods section: 218 universities matched across THE, ARWU, CWUR, QS and OpenAlex by normalised name. Count-up on scroll into view.
des_scale.rationale: The scale of the analysis is a concrete number worth surfacing once in the methods appendix; a stat callout is lighter than a chart for a single figure.

page_rhythm.accent_meaning: Gilt gold = the crown / the #1 that keeps changing hands. It is the story's one bold idea: the same gold highlights the moving champion in the bump chart, the reputation half in the weights bar, the plunging line in the size-flip, and the reweighter's live #1 card.
page_rhythm.accent_secondary_meaning: Cool teal = the NEUTRAL OpenAlex referee, kept visually distinct from the gold 'commercial crown' wherever the referee appears (bump chart's OpenAlex column, referee scatter/lollipop).

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial, cinematic, scholarly-nocturne — a premium data-journalism page that reads like an evening in a library.
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: Visual-first at the two tentpoles (the animated hero + hook chart in edt_01; the reweighter centerpiece in edt_06) and text-forward through the analytical middle (edt_02, edt_05, edt_09), where each chart is a quiet piece of evidence rather than a spectacle. Real campus photography and the cinematic scroll thread between beats so the page feels reported.
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: No chart streak — nine distinct forms (bump, heatmap, dumbbell/range, 100%-stacked bar, diverging bar, scatter, grouped lollipop, 2-point slope, dot plot), each earning its section. A single gilt-gold crown accent + a night-campus cinematic + a nocturne BGM give a scholarly-cinematic identity that avoids both the generic-AI dashboard look and the templated bootstrap-blue hero. High-contrast Didot display over a sturdy Georgia body is a deliberate, non-default pairing.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Didot display reserved for h1/h2 at large sizes (3x+ size jumps, weight extremes — thin display over heavy stat numbers); Georgia for running analytical body; system-ui for chart labels, slider UI and the now-playing card. Finishes (apply with restraint): gold uppercase KICKERS above section titles; ONE drop cap on the article lead; HAIRLINE dividers only (serious/quant); NO paper grain (this is a dark data page); an oversized-serif PULL QUOTE for the closing line 'the number-one university is not a fact waiting to be discovered; it is an answer you get to configure.' Count-up on the big stat numbers (89-place swing, +331 flip, 218 core).
page_rhythm.motion_notes: Drive all motion from the motion.json :root tokens; animate transform/opacity only; respect prefers-reduced-motion (one switch). Hero cinemagraph loops seamlessly (boomerang). Sections scroll-reveal with the visible-by-default guardrail (gate opacity behind html.js-reveal, EXCLUDE charts/figures so async Vega never stays blank; never gate above the fold). Bump/slope/dumbbell lines draw in on reveal (--dur-lg, --ease-out). Reweighter: slider drags recompute INSTANTLY (--dur-xs crossfade on the leaderboard, no flicker) because dragging is high-frequency; only the crown badge pops gently (--ease-spring, once) when the champion actually flips. Number count-ups use --dur-count. Never autoplay the BGM.
page_rhythm.centerpiece_flag_for_interaction_enginee: edt_06 / des_reweighter — the one explorable the reader must PRODUCE. The six supporting playgrounds are the Editor's curated interactives block (img_04 scored quiz @edt_01, img_03 guess-then-reveal @edt_03, img_11 scored quiz @edt_04, img_07 toggle-the-referee @edt_07 [carries ana_08's three-way self-disagreement], img_05 guess-then-reveal @edt_08, img_02 personal-input lookup @edt_10) — each bound to a distinct finding.
